thread:
leila: FYI I launched a broad bring-up comparing rerank-v4-ptq (int8) vs rerank-v4-fp16 on web-qa-v2. seeing a localized MRR bump in short queries but NDCG dip in long queries. logs attached to the run.
omar: link? what cohorting did you use? did you stratify by query length or locale? :mag:
leila: run command:```
./eval_runner --model rerank-v4-ptq --baseline rerank-v4-fp16 --dataset web-qa-v2 --seed 11 --n_queries 25000 --cohorts short,mid,long --stratify query_length --bootstrap 1000
```
rui: top-level aggregated: overall NDCG@5: int8 0.702 / fp16 0.705; MRR@1: int8 0.489 / fp16 0.478. so int8 improves MRR but loses slight NDCG.
leila: breakdown by length bins:
- short(<5 tokens): NDCG@5 int8 0.673 / fp16 0.660 ; MRR int8 0.612 / fp16 0.587
- mid(5-20): NDCG@5 int8 0.711 / fp16 0.714 ; MRR int8 0.495 / fp16 0.492
- long(>20): NDCG@5 int8 0.722 / fp16 0.736 ; MRR int8 0.382 / fp16 0.389
qa: p-values (paired bootstrap) for bins: short p=0.004 (MRR lift), mid p=0.21 (ns), long NDCG drop p=0.018.
omar: interesting — int8 helps short queries' top-1 but harms ranking depth for long queries. could be truncation or context shifting. did you check candidate truncation policy?
leila: yes, eval used default candidate_trunc=2048 tokens, query_trunc=1024. long queries often push candidate context partial. suspect priming/context order interacts with quant kernels.
rui: do score distributions show compression? e.g., top1-top2 margin per bin?
leila: margins: short int8 +0.07 vs fp16 +0.04; mid int8 +0.05 vs +0.05; long int8 +0.02 vs +0.06. so int8 reduces separation on long queries.
omar: could be numeric underflow/quantization of logits for longer contexts. we should run with float32 accumulation or mixed-precision matmuls as a check. add flag --accum-fp32.
leila: kicked off a job with --accum-fp32 on long bin only. also trying dynamic_padding=false to avoid extra token shifts.
qa: also consider dataset sampling bias: web-qa-v2 long bin has more code-like docs and multi-paragraph answers. maybe reranker training distribution mismatch.
rui: do we have tokenizer parity between eval and production scorer? tokenizer mismatch can change effective length buckets.
leila: tokenizer versions: eval uses tok v2.1, production uses v2.0. created a quick run with tok=v2.0 to compare.
omar: if differences persist after accum-fp32 and tokenizer parity, run a small ablation on candidate ordering (swap doc vs passage-first) to see if context window hits are ordering dependent.
leila: scheduled ablation. also sampled 40 long queries where top3 changed; manual review: 22/40 looked worse under int8, mostly where long reasoning snippets got truncated mid-sentence. 12 neutral, 6 better.
qa: bootstrap CI on those 40: int8 worse by NDCG@5 mean -0.028, 95% CI [-0.045, -0.012].
rui: suggests a real user-visible regression for long queries. mitigation ideas: (1) prefer fp16 for long-query customers, (2) adopt hybrid strategy: route long queries to dedicated fp16 pool, short to int8, (3) model-level quant tweaks (per-channel scaling).
omar: routing sounds pragmatic. can we detect long-form semantics reliably? use a lightweight classifier at proxy.
leila: created an RFC draft for hybrid routing + evalmetadata flag "quant_bucket". will push soon.
qa: one more ask: add template_id & tokenizer_version and candidate_trunc to eval metadata so smaller follow-ups can filter. open a tiny PR?
rui: I'll own the PR.
leila: thanks. will post updated numbers when accum-fp32 and tokenizer-parity runs finish (~3h). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
